programs.title: Helical Circle Pocket
programs.description: Mills a round pocket by ramping down on a helix instead of plunging straight down. Great first practice program for getting comfortable with G2/G3 arcs and tool length offsets.
programs.code:
%
O1001 (HELICAL CIRCLE POCKET)
(TOOL 1: 1/2 IN FLAT ENDMILL)
G20 G17 G40 G49 G80 G90
G28 G91 Z0.
G90
T1 M6
G54
S3500 M3
G0 X0. Y0.
G43 H1 Z1. M8
G1 Z0.1 F20.
G91
G3 X-0.5 Y0. Z-0.6 I-0.5 J0. F12.
G3 I0.5 J0.
G3 I0.5 J0.
G3 I0.5 J0.
G90
G0 Z1.
M9
G91 G28 Z0.
M30
%
notes: I/J values define the arc center relative to the start point — keep them consistent for a true circle.
Each G3 loop drops Z by a small amount (helical ramp) until full depth is reached, then one final full-circle pass cleans the floor.
Increase the I/J radius and number of loops to cut a larger pocket with the same endmill.

programs.title: Hexagonal Pocket (Cutter Comp)
programs.description: Cuts a regular hexagon pocket using G41 cutter compensation, with a lead-in/lead-out arc so the tool enters and exits the wall smoothly without a witness mark.
notes: G41 D2 turns on left-side cutter compensation using the diameter stored in offset register D2.
The G3 ... R0.5 moves are quarter-circle lead-in and lead-out arcs — never turn cutter comp on or off with a straight plunge into the wall.
Each G1 segment is one of the six hexagon sides; rotate the X/Y values to make a different polygon (pentagon, octagon, etc.).

programs.title: Bolt Hole Circle Drilling
programs.description: Drills a ring of equally-spaced holes (a flange bolt pattern) using the Haas G70 bolt-hole-circle canned cycle combined with a peck drilling cycle.
programs.code:
%
O1003 (BOLT HOLE CIRCLE - 6 HOLES)
(TOOL 3: #7 DRILL)
G20 G17 G40 G49 G80 G90
G28 G91 Z0.
G90
T3 M6
G54
S2200 M3
G0 X0. Y0.
G43 H3 Z1. M8
G99 G83 Z-0.6 R0.1 Q0.15 F8.
G70 X0. Y0. Z-0.6 I2.0 J0. K6 L0
G80
G0 Z1.
M9
G91 G28 Z0.
M30
%
notes: G70 X_ Y_ I_ J_ K_ — X/Y is the bolt circle center, I is the circle radius, J is the start angle, K is the number of holes (evenly spaced).
G83 is a peck drilling cycle: Q sets the peck increment so chips clear from a deep hole.
Always cancel canned cycles with G80 before moving to the next operation.

programs.title: Drilling Grid Pattern
programs.description: Drills a 3x3 grid of through-holes — a classic plate program for practicing positioning moves and a simple canned drilling cycle.
notes: The first G81 line sets up the cycle (depth Z, retract plane R, feed F); every line after that just repeats the cycle at a new X/Y.
R0.1 is the retract (rapid plane) above the part — keep it just clear of clamps and the part surface.
Change the X/Y increments to match your bolt spacing, or generate them from CAM for larger grids.

programs.title: Spiral Pocket (R-Parameter Loop)
programs.description: Uses Sinumerik R-parameters and a GOTOB loop to mill an outward spiral, growing the arc radius on every pass until the pocket reaches full size — a compact alternative to programming dozens of separate arcs.
notes: R1 is the current spiral radius, R2 is the final radius, and R3 is how much the radius grows on each lap.
The GOTOB LOOP1 line jumps back to the LOOP1: label as long as R1 is still smaller than R2, generating one continuous spiral.
Because each pass overlaps the previous one by (R3 / tool diameter), keep R3 small relative to the cutter to avoid leaving uncut ridges.

programs.title: 5-Point Star Engraving
programs.description: Traces a 5-point star outline with a V-bit at a shallow engraving depth — a fun, attractive pattern for testing tool offsets and engraving feeds before running a real nameplate job.
notes: A 60-degree V-bit gives a crisp engraved line at a very shallow Z depth (here only 0.02 in) — too deep and the line becomes too wide.
The X/Y points trace the five outer tips and five inner notches of the star in one continuous loop.
Slow the feed rate (F) further for harder materials or smaller V-bit angles to avoid chipping the point of the tool.

programs.title: Rectangular Contour Profile
programs.description: Profiles the outside of a rectangular plate using G42 cutter compensation with a tangential lead-in/out arc — the standard way to cut a finished outline to size.
notes: G42 D6 applies right-side cutter compensation using diameter offset register D6 — use G41 instead if cutting the part on the other side of the tool path.
Each corner uses a small G3 fillet (R0.5) so the tool decelerates smoothly instead of stopping dead at a sharp corner.
Run this in graphics/verify mode first — incorrect comp direction (G41 vs G42) will cut the part oversize or undersize.

programs.title: Face Milling (Zig-Zag Passes)
programs.description: Squares up the top of a stock block with a back-and-forth (zig-zag) facing pattern using a large face mill — usually the very first operation in a setup.
notes: Step over by roughly 60-70% of the face mill diameter so each pass overlaps the last and leaves no ridges.
Take a light depth of cut (0.02-0.05 in) for facing — the goal is a flat, clean surface, not heavy stock removal.
Start the first pass off the edge of the stock so the cutter enters the air, not directly into material.

programs.title: Slot Milling with Ramp Entry
programs.description: Mills a closed slot by ramping the endmill diagonally into the material instead of plunging straight down — much easier on the tool and spindle.

G28 G91 Z0.
G90

G54

G1 X1.0 Z-0.4 F25.
G1 X-1.0
G1 X1.0
G0 Z0.5
M9
G91 G28 Z0.

%
notes: The first cut moves both X and Z at once — that diagonal move is the ramp, ending exactly at full slot depth.
Once at depth, run one or more straight passes back and forth to clean up the slot floor and walls.
If the slot is narrower than the cutter diameter, this becomes a simple groove; widen the X travel for a wider pocket.

programs.title: Lathe OD Turning + Threading
programs.description: A complete two-tool lathe program: G71 rough turns a stepped shaft to a finish profile, G70 finishes it, then a second tool cuts a 60-degree thread with G76.
notes: G71 P10 Q20 U0.5 W0.1 F0.25 rough-turns everything between blocks N10 and N20, leaving 0.5mm on diameter and 0.1mm on the face for the finish pass.
G70 P10 Q20 re-runs the same N10-N20 profile at finishing speed/feed to clean up to the final dimension.
G76 P010060 Q50 R0.05 sets a 60-degree thread angle with a 0.05mm finishing allowance; the next G76 line gives the thread's final X diameter, Z length, depth (P) and first-pass depth (Q).
